declarations.provides: The maximal subgroupoid of a category, the groupoid of isomorphisms that the plus comparison localises.
The idempotent completion, the standard witness that cofinality changes the group in degree zero.
The property that a category admits filtered colimits. This does not construct filtered colimits of categories or prove their nerve compatibility; those are StableHomotopyKTheory H.1 inputs.
The generic existence property for pushouts. Waldhausen data require chosen pushouts only along cofibrations, not this stronger all-pushouts property.
Serre classes in an abelian category, the hypothesis of Quillen's localisation theorem; the localisation long exact sequence itself is absent.
The nerve of a category, the first ingredient of the K-theory space.
The homotopy groups of a pointed space, the third; no K-theory space is built from these three at the pins.
The complement is the image of the complementary idempotent, the other half.
A finitely generated projective module is a retract of a finite free module, the module-theoretic half of K.2:plus's cofinality node.

Extension of scalars between module categories, pinned between commutative rings only. The functor along an arbitrary unital ring map is KTheoryLowDegrees:Z.1/extend-scalars, which agrees with this one for commutative rings; K.2:plus cites this declaration only for that comparison.
The realisation of a simplicial set, the second ingredient.
The canonical unitisation of a nonunital ring with its universal property, exactly the unitisation K.5 specifies; nothing K-theoretic is built on it at the pins.
The Grothendieck group of an exact category, which the fundamental-group theorem of K.1 identifies with the first homotopy group of the Q-construction.
Invariance of that group under an exact equivalence, likewise.
The comparison of the Grothendieck groups of two exact structures on one category, which the audit records is NOT cofinality; K.3's cofinality node says so.
Invariance of that group under the transport, the degree-zero form of the independence K.1 states in every degree.

Quillen exact structures on an additive category, with conflations and admissible monomorphisms and epimorphisms. This is the stated input of K.1 and it is fully built; the Q-construction is built ON it, not instead of it.
Every additive functor is conflation-exact for split exact structures. This is why scalar extension on finitely generated projectives needs no flatness hypothesis, which is what K.2:plus asks for.

The degree-zero resolution isomorphism, proved under the stronger hypothesis that every resolving object is projective; K.3 states the general theorem in every degree and cites this as the pinned special case.
Transport of an exact structure along an additive equivalence, the pinned half of K.1's small-model target.
The instance of that isomorphism for modules with finite projective resolutions.
The Grothendieck group of finitely generated modules over an artinian ring is free on the simple classes, which is devissage in degree zero; K.3 states the theorem in every degree.

Object property of finitely generated projective R-modules, R : Type u. Its full subcategory has an anonymous EssentiallySmall.{u} instance in this pinned file (CartanMap.lean, section 'Essential smallness'; not indexed by name), which fixes the universe of ExactK0 and of K(R) at u.
Existing exact structure on the full subcategory of finitely generated projectives; import this carrier rather than reconstruct it.
The induced exact structure is equal to the split structure. This is the input that makes arbitrary scalar extension exact on projectives.
Conflations are exactly short exact sequences after inclusion in ModuleCat R.
Existing object-class map to ExactK0; the π₁ comparison must preserve this map.
Existing conflation-additivity relation for the class map.
Existing universal property: conflation-additive invariants are additive homomorphisms out of ExactK0.
The homomorphism out of ExactK0 induced by a conflation-additive invariant; the map from ExactK0 to the fundamental group of the Q-construction is this lift of the two-edge loops.
Two homomorphisms out of ExactK0 agreeing on object classes are equal; it checks one composite of the fundamental-group comparison.

An isomorphism-invariant, conflation-additive function on objects with values in an abelian group: the datum ExactK0.lift consumes. Its values must lie in a commutative group, which is why the fundamental-group node proves commutativity before lifting.
Base change of a conflation along any morphism is a conflation with the same kernel: the admissible-epimorphism half of composition in Q, and the dual step of the exact category of conflations.
Cobase change of a conflation along any morphism is a conflation with the same cokernel (Bühler, Proposition 2.12); an input of the 3×3 lemma and of the exact category of conflations.

The pullback of a deflation along an inflation is a kernel of the composite deflation, so the pullback of an admissible monomorphism along an admissible epimorphism is an admissible monomorphism (Bühler, Proposition 2.15). It is the admissible-monomorphism half of composition in Q and is proved from E1op and the kernel property alone, without Quillen's axiom (c).
The Noether isomorphism for a composite of two inflations (Bühler, Lemma 3.5), the last step of the 3×3 lemma.
A pushout of an inflation is a bicartesian square (Bühler, Proposition 2.12), used in the 3×3 lemma.
A biproduct of two conflations is a conflation; it makes the coproduct functor into the exact category of conflations exact.

The category of conflations of an exact structure: the full subcategory of short complexes on the conflations, with its three projection functors and functoriality in conflation-exact functors. It is the carrier of the extension category E(A) that K.3 makes exact; the pinned file puts no exact structure on it.
The pullback of two ring maps as a subring of the product, for arbitrary (noncommutative) rings: the ring B of a Milnor square.
The pullback square of rings commutes, which makes the composite of the first two maps of the Milnor sequence vanish.
The quotient of a possibly noncommutative ring by a two-sided ideal ([I.IsTwoSided]) is a ring; it is the quotient map through which K.5 treats a pair (A, I) without narrowing to commutative rings.
The canonical exact structure of all short exact sequences on an abelian category: the ambient structure of Gillet–Waldhausen's closure hypothesis, where the ambient abelian category is data.

The exact structure induced on an extension-closed full subcategory; with ExactStructure.abelian it presents an exact category inside a given abelian category, the form in which the K-book's Definition II.7.0 is used here.
Equivalence of categories, the hypothesis of the invariance statements; the enhanced version K.7 needs is not pinned and the comparison node says so.
Triangulated subcategories, pinned; the input to a Verdier quotient, which is not itself pinned.
The class of maps whose cone lies in a triangulated subcategory, pinned; the morphisms a Verdier quotient inverts.
The Morita equivalence predicate, pinned; K.7 supplies the K-theoretic consequence, which is absent.
The instance that a ring is Morita equivalent to its matrix ring, pinned and cited by the invariance node.
Nilpotence of an element (some power is zero), the condition on the endomorphisms of the Nil category.
The Laurent polynomial ring, the third term of that sequence and the ring whose K-theory the fundamental theorem decomposes.
Matrices, out of which the cone ring and the infinite matrix ring of the flasque and axiom nodes are built.
The category of modules over a ring, not necessarily commutative; the components of the glued triples of the projective line over a ring live in it.
The equivalence between modules over a ring and modules over its matrix ring, which is the pinned form of the Morita instance K.7 cites.
The polynomial ring in one variable, one of the two rings in the four-term sequence that defines the contraction.
Ring maps, the morphisms of the functors this layer defines.
The tensor product, the biexact functor from which the external products of K.7 are built.
The Frobenius condition on an exact structure, PINNED in Tau Ceti: it is the hypothesis of the second construction of K.6, and the packet cites it rather than defining it again.
The split exact structure is Frobenius, pinned; it is the degenerate unit test of the Frobenius-pair node.
The split model of the zeroth K-group, in which the pinned product statement is proved.
The pinned statement that the product of the classes of two objects is the class of their tensor product, the degree-zero unit test of K.7's product.

summary: Unified target-level plan for exact, Waldhausen, relative and nonconnective algebraic K-theory. The two existing part packets remain the canonical owners of their 156 node IDs; this main packet imports those targets and supplies the additional routed-source interfaces. Exact structures, exact K0, finite projectives, unitization and module Morita equivalences are reused from the pinned libraries. All implementation statuses are unchecked. Open supplier contracts, source-proof gaps and stage-order proposals are recorded explicitly; no acceptance verdict is inherited.

nodes.title: The symmetric monoidal projective model
nodes.statement: For a unital ring R, let P(R)^≃ be the maximal groupoid of finitely generated projective right R-modules with direct sum. Its symmetric monoidal group completion is a connective spectrum K⊕(R). There is a natural equivalence Ω∞K⊕(R)≃ΩBQ(P(R)), and after S-spectrum assembly an equivalence of connective spectra K⊕(R)≃Kconn(R). The comparison takes an object P to its ExactK0 class and its automorphisms to their K1 classes.
hypotheses: The exact structure is the pinned split exact finite-projective structure, transported to right modules through Rᵒᵖ. Use the core, not the category of all module maps.
Symmetric monoidal group completion, spectra and their recognition are H.4/H.5 inputs. Tensor product is a separate biexact operation; direct sum is the group-completed operation.
proofSteps: Apply H.4 group completion to the essentially small core with direct sum.
Use the existing free-module cofinality and plus–Q comparison, matching the object and stabilized automorphism maps.
Use the S–Q comparison and H.5 recognition to promote the infinite-loop-space comparison to connective spectra, naturally in arbitrary unital ring maps.

nodes.title: Excision data and Milnor squares
nodes.statement: An excision datum consists of a unital ring map f:A→B, two-sided ideals I⊂A and J⊂B, and the requirement that f restrict to an isomorphism I≅J of nonunital rings. The quotient square A→B, A/I→B/J is both a pullback and a pushout in unital rings and has surjective quotient maps. For a functor F to spectra, excision on this datum means that its square is homotopy cartesian, equivalently fib(F(A)→F(A/I))→fib(F(B)→F(B/J)) is an equivalence.
hypotheses: The algebraic datum is allowed for associative rings. The domain-base-change theorem below is restricted to commutative rings.
An arbitrary pullback of rings without a surjective side is not called a Milnor square here.
proofSteps: Use RingHom.pullback for the underlying ring pullback. The ideal identification proves that A maps bijectively to the pullback.
The common ideal kills the difference between the two quotient descriptions; the universal property proves the pushout assertion.
Use the generic fibre/pullback equivalence for spectra. Keep the datum separate from the assertion that K-theory satisfies excision on it.

nodes.title: Excision data after domain base change
nodes.statement: If (A,I)→(B,J) is a commutative excision datum and A→V is a map to an integral domain, then the tensor-base-changed quotient square is again a Milnor square: V→(B⊗_A V)×_((B/J)⊗_A V)((A/I)⊗_A V) is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: All rings in the datum are commutative; V is an integral domain. No flatness is required of A→V.
proofSteps: Tensor the right-exact sequence for the original Milnor square; this gives surjectivity onto the new pullback.
The kernel is an ideal of V. If its localization to Frac(V) is zero, torsion-freeness makes it zero.
Over the fraction field the image of I is either zero or the unit ideal, and in either case the tensor square is a pullback. This proves injectivity.

nodes.title: Tor-unital nonunital rings
nodes.statement: For an associative nonunital ring I, put I⁺=Z⋉I using the pinned Unitization. Call I Tor-unital if the multiplication Z⊗^L_(I⁺)Z→Z is an equivalence, or equivalently Tor_n^(I⁺)(Z,Z)=0 for every n>0. The two Z modules use the augmentation I⁺→Z. This is integral Tor-unitality, not only bar acyclicity after tensoring with Q.
hypotheses: Tensor factors are a right and a left I⁺-module; noncommutative rings are allowed.
The degree-zero tensor map is already an isomorphism, and Tor1 identifies with I/I². Derived tensor is imported from the enhanced module supplier.
proofSteps: Use the canonical augmentation of Unitization and its augmentation ideal.
Apply the augmentation short exact sequence to identify Tor1 with I/I².
Identify the higher homology of the derived tensor with Tor, giving the equivalent criterion.

nodes.title: Flat idempotent ideals are Tor-unital
nodes.statement: If a nonunital ring I is flat as a right module over I⁺ and I²=I, then I is Tor-unital. More generally a two-sided ideal I in a unital ring A that is flat as a right A-module and idempotent makes A→A/I Tor-unital. To deduce intrinsic Tor-unitality from the second statement, apply it to A=I⁺ or use a separately justified change-of-unitization criterion.
hypotheses: Flatness must be over the ring in the Tor calculation; idempotence alone only kills Tor1.
proofSteps: The exact sequence 0→I→A→A/I→0 and flatness give a flat resolution of length one.
Tensor with A/I. The resulting degree-one term is I/I²=0 and higher terms vanish.

Set A=I⁺ for the intrinsic version. The filtered-multiplication model in the Berkovich consumer supplies flatness over its chosen unital model and the canonical-unitization comparison must be retained.

nodes.title: Suslin excision via the derived square
nodes.statement: For an associative Tor-unital nonunital ring I and every unital A containing I as a two-sided ideal, the canonical map Knc(I):=fib(Knc(I⁺)→Knc(Z))→fib(Knc(A)→Knc(A/I)) is an equivalence of spectra. Thus nonunital K-theory is independent of the ambient ring under this hypothesis. The induced comparison of classical relative groups is an isomorphism in every nonnegative degree.
hypotheses: Use nonconnective K-theory for the spectrum statement. Agreement with the classical models is supplied by K.6 and Part II.
No converse or finite-degree Tor criterion is inferred from Tamme’s sufficiency theorem.
proofSteps: The square I⁺→Z, A→A/I is a homotopy pullback of E1-ring spectra, since its quotient maps are surjective.

Tor-unitality and Tamme Lemma 23 identify Z⊗^L_(I⁺)A with A/I. Apply the Part II replacement-algebra theorem: its replacement algebra has this underlying spectrum and the canonical multiplication is an equivalence of E1-rings.
The replacement square is cartesian under every localizing invariant, in particular Knc. Taking horizontal fibres proves the assertion.
Equivalently Tamme’s direct proof uses the lax-pullback exact sequence of perfect categories. Do not replace this by the generally false claim that Perf(A)→Perf(A/I) is a Verdier localization.

nodes.title: Dedekind localization and primary torsion
nodes.statement: Let R be a Dedekind domain with fraction field K and S a set of nonzero prime ideals. Define R_S={x∈K | v_p(x)≥0 for every nonzero p outside S}. It is the filtered union of the invertible fractional ideals R_D for effective divisors D supported on S, where R_D allows the pole orders specified by D. Let T_S be the abelian category of finitely generated R-modules killed by some finite product of powers of primes in S, and Perf_S(R) the perfect complexes with homology in T_S.
hypotheses: The elements of S are prime ideals, not chosen prime elements. Without a class-group hypothesis R_S need not be presented by inverting one chosen element per prime.
T_S objects have finite support even when S is infinite. Finite type and torsion are required.
proofSteps: Use the valuation description of fractional ideals to form R_D and their directed union. It proves flatness of R_S and R_S⊗_R R_S≅R_S.
Finite generation identifies torsion objects with finite sums of p-primary modules. The Serre conditions follow by checking subobjects, quotients and extensions.
Use global dimension one to identify the bounded derived category of T_S with the full perfect support category; establish the bounded torsion t-structure.

nodes.title: Dedekind Poincaré localization
nodes.statement: For a Dedekind domain R, an invertible R-module M with involution and a set S of nonzero primes, Perf_S(R)→Perf(R)→Perf(R_S) is a Poincaré–Verdier sequence for each structure Q_M^≥m, m∈Z∪{−∞,+∞}. Hence the associated Grothendieck–Witt and L spectra have the support localization fibre sequences. This does not identify the support term with residue fields in the quadratic flavour.
hypotheses: Use the actual Poincaré structures and Verdier/localization machinery from GN.6/HK.0; exact-category Qʰ alone does not supply them.
No invertibility-of-two assumption. Localization before devissage is valid for the flavour family.
proofSteps: The flat localization R→R_S is a derived localization and its fibre is generated by perfect torsion objects from R_D/R.
Use divisor classes to show Pic(R)→Pic(R_S) and hence K0(R)→K0(R_S) are surjective.
Apply the generic Poincaré localization criterion with the induced coefficient and shift; its K0 condition is now checked.

nodes.title: Shifted duality on the torsion heart
nodes.statement: On Perf_S(R), the duality RHom_R(−,M[1]) restricts to T_S and is canonically T↦Hom_R(T,M_S/M), where M_S=R_S⊗_R M. In the symmetric flavour the induced space of forms on a torsion-heart object is discrete and identifies with symmetric bilinear linking pairings valued in M_S/M; the nondegenerate forms correspond to perfect such pairings.
hypotheses: R is Dedekind, M is an invertible line with involution, and T has finite S-primary support. The shift by +1 is essential.
Discreteness is a statement about the space of symmetric forms on heart objects, not that the entire Poincaré structure spectrum is discrete.
proofSteps: Apply RHom_R(T,−) to M→M_S→M_S/M. The middle term has no maps or higher Ext from T.
Global dimension one and injectivity of the divisible coefficient identify the resulting shifted dual with ordinary Hom on T_S.
Take the symmetric homotopy fixed-point form space. Its nonnegative homotopy is concentrated in degree zero on these objects, giving the linking-pairing description.

nodes.title: The exact-versus-split fibre
nodes.statement: For a small idempotent-complete exact category E, let E⊕ carry its split exact structure and let fpEff(E) be the abelian category of finitely presented effaceable additive functors Eᵒᵖ→Ab. There is a natural fibre sequence IK(fpEff(E))→IK(E⊕)→IK(E). For a general small E first take the idempotent completion. hypotheses: Effaceable means every map from a representable is killed by precomposition with a deflation. Use the enhanced/Frobenius models, not only triangle equivalences.
proofSteps: A finitely presented effaceable functor has a projective resolution 0→A→B→C→F→0 coming from a conflation in E. This proves that fpEff(E) is abelian and extension closed.

Let Ê consist of extensions of objects of fpEff(E) by representables. It is extension closed in Mod(E). The displayed finite resolutions and Keller’s fully exact resolution criterion identify Dᵇ(E⊕) with Dᵇ(Ê).

For fpEff(E)⊂Ê, verify the dual criterion by lifting the representable subobject across a deflation; the resulting cokernel remains effaceable. Thus Dᵇ(fpEff(E)) embeds fully faithfully with image the acyclic E complexes. Lemma 11.7 passes the bounded/unbounded cofinality step used by Theorem 12.1.

Apply the Frobenius-pair localization theorem to these enhanced comparisons. The source’s conditional consequence assuming general abelian vanishing remains conditional; Neeman’s counterexamples prevent treating that assumption as a theorem.

restructure.title: The localisation theorems of K.3 and K.4 are different theorems and should stay apart
restructure.detail: K.3's stage text warns against asserting localisation for arbitrary exact subcategories. This packet honours that by keeping Quillen's theorem, which is for a Serre subcategory of an abelian category, in K.3, and the Waldhausen theorem, which needs a cylinder functor with the cylinder axiom and saturation and extension for the larger class, in K.4. The two stage texts should each point at the other, because a reader who finds only one of them will be tempted to use it outside its hypotheses; that is exactly the error the K.3 text names.

restructure.detail: AUDIT-28 records SchemeKTheoryOperations S.5 as duplicating K.6's fundamental theorem and S.6 as duplicating K.7's external products. Read against the source these are not duplications but the ring and scheme forms of the same theorem, and the source states them separately for exactly that reason: V.8.2 for rings and V.8.3 for quasi-projective schemes. The resolution is that the ring form, with its ring-level inputs (the projective line over an associative ring, the Nil groups, the localisation at t), is proved in this roadmap, and the scheme roadmap imports it for its scheme forms: S.5 and S.6 come after K.6 and K.7 in the atlas, so no node here may cite them (RT-AREA-ktheory-1/17 found the former prerequisite S.5 → K.6 closing a cycle). restructure.title: K.6 carries two independent developments and could be split
restructure.detail: K.6's stage text asks both for Bass's negative groups, which need only the zeroth and first K-groups and no homotopy theory, and for the Fundamental Theorem in every degree and the nonconnective spectrum, which need connective K-theory spaces, spectra, homotopy colimits and connective covers, none of which exists in either pinned library. The first part is formalisable against the pins today; the second is blocked on a library of spectra. As one layer it cannot be closed until the homotopy theory arrives, and a reader cannot see that the algebraic part is independently available. Splitting into a negative-K-groups layer and a nonconnective layer would make that visible. Along that line the Bass-side nodes divide as follows: flasque rings, contracted functors, the negative groups, the axioms and the Mayer–Vietoris continuation go to the first layer (their degree-zero and degree-one inputs being the classical K_0 and K_1); the projective line over a ring and its splitting, the Nil groups, the localisation sequences at t, Nil_n ≅ NK_{n+1}, the Fundamental Theorem in positive degrees and its splitting, the contractedness of the K-groups, the Bass spectrum and its homotopy groups, the spectrum form of Milnor-square excision and the vanishing theorem go to the second.

A name such as IsFlasqueRing, or Karoubi's own terminology of an infinite sum ring where that stronger notion suffices, should be fixed before any of this layer is written.

First, the comparison in degree zero: the product of the classes of two finitely generated projective modules is the class of their tensor product, so that the map from the tensor square of the zeroth K-group to itself is determined on classes; Tau Ceti has exactly this statement for the split model and it is cited as baseline.
